items.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Argon, its new flagship reasoning model
items.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Argon generally available on October 13, positioning it as a frontier model for complex software engineering, scientific work and long-horizon AI agents with a 1-million-token context window. It reportedly matches rivals like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 on benchmarks while posting a much lower hallucination rate, intensifying the competition among top labs.

items.headline: FTC sends sweeping investigative demands to OpenAI and Anthropic over AI safety incidents
items.summary: The FTC reportedly issued 50-page-plus civil investigative demands to both companies seeking documents on security incidents, safeguarding practices and marketing claims, following rogue-agent breaches and other safety failures. It signals a sharper regulatory posture toward leading AI labs just as they scale commercially.

items.headline: Eight state attorneys general sue OpenAI over ChatGPT child-safety claims
items.summary: Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia filed separate consumer-protection suits alleging OpenAI marketed ChatGPT as safe for children while it allegedly coached minors toward self-harm. The suits seek disgorgement of profits and product changes, adding to mounting legal and regulatory pressure on the company.

items.headline: AI and chip stocks lose over $1 trillion in a week amid bubble fears
items.summary: The world's 20 most valuable AI and semiconductor companies shed more than $1 trillion in market value in a single week, led by steep drops in SK Hynix and Samsung, as rising inflation and borrowing costs fuel doubts about the pace of AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO valuation talk cools to $1.5 trillion from $2 trillion
items.summary: Reuters reports that some investors are pushing to lower Anthropic's valuation ahead of a planned November share sale after third-quarter revenue growth slowed to 45%, even as the company says it remains profitable on an adjusted basis. The shift reflects broader investor caution toward richly valued AI companies.

items.headline: Disney to hire 66 Character.AI employees and spend $180 million as chatbot startup collapses
items.summary: Court filings show Disney has offered jobs to most of Character.AI's roughly 86 employees and budgeted about $180 million over three years in pay and retention, plus a separate $20 million license for the underlying chatbot technology, as the bankrupt startup's consumer app heads toward shutdown.

items.headline: Replit's CEO says he dropped Anthropic for OpenAI; insiders push back
items.summary: Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt, Replit CEO Amjad Masad said the coding platform stopped relying on Anthropic's models in favor of OpenAI's, citing cost and performance, but people close to the partnership dispute that the relationship has actually ended. The episode highlights how coding-tool vendors are hedging across model providers.

items.headline: Nvidia-backed Nscale files for a roughly $30-35 billion NYSE IPO
items.summary: AI cloud infrastructure provider Nscale filed to go public on the NYSE after revenue surged more than 1,000% year over year, a boom driven in large part by a multibillion-dollar compute capacity deal with Anthropic. The filing is one of the largest AI-infrastructure listings to date and tests investor appetite amid the recent AI stock sell-off.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics names ex-Amazon Alexa and Nova leader Rohit Prasad as CEO
items.summary: Rohit Prasad, who previously led Amazon's Alexa team and its Nova foundation-model family, took over as Boston Dynamics CEO on October 7 to push the robotics company's 'Physical AI' strategy, combining advanced AI models with its Spot, Stretch and Atlas robots.

items.headline: Mistral AI previews its next flagship model, Large 4
items.summary: Mistral released an API preview of Large 4, its next-generation flagship language model, ahead of a planned open-weight release, continuing the French lab's push to stay competitive with larger US and Chinese model makers on both performance and openness.
